newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere shares ease on Thomson doubts.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere shares ease on Thomson doubts.

text.p: Shares in Lagardere underperformed the Paris bourse on Friday as investors wondered whether it would succeed in acquiring Thomson SA's defence electronics activities, set to be sold off by the government as part of the relaunch of the botched Thomson privatisation.
Analysts said they still believe Lagardere is the favoured candidate to acquire Thomson-CSF because the French government wants to create a French defence champion.
"The market's not sure. The process will be more open and we can't rule out other bidders," a trader said. Lagardere shares were down 2.7 percent at 146.50 francs at 1530 GMT.
The market's CAC-40 index was down 0.7 percent.
The share rallied in October when the government said it favoured Lagardere's bid for Thomson over a rival offer from Alcatel Alsthom.

But the government suspended the process this month after France's independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of Lagardere's proposed sale of the Thomson Multimedia branch to Korea's Daewoo Electronic for one franc.
The government this week said it would relaunch the privatisation of Thomson, selling Thomson-CSF first and then Thomson Multimedia after a recapitalisation.

Lagardere shares, which were trading at 133 francs before the government announced it was the favoured candidate, rose to 177.80 francs as the market applauded the creation of a defence electronics giant comprising Thomson-CSF and Lagardere's Matra missiles unit.

Traders said that now that Thomson was no longer being sold in one block, smaller players might decide to join the bidding. They cited Dassault Aviation, Dassault Electronique, state-owned Aerospatiale, Sagem and Compagnie des Signaux as possible bidders.
